The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 22.05.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 22.05.2024 at about 6.30 to 6.40 p.m., the petitioner was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 52-J-8860 in front of Milk Dairy, on Kanakapura - Kodihalli road, Gabbadi illage, Harohalli Taluk, Ramanagara District, SCCH-10 at that time, the driver of the Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-4898 came with with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's bike.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
The respondent No.1 being owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present petition.
3. Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
In pursuance to the Petition notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
SCCH-10 4.

The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 being insurer of offending vehicle has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Swift Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-4898 in the name of respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident,

sentences.text: Further, the respondent No.2 has denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, the petitioner has filed the false case against the offending vehicle for wrongful loss to this respondent.

Further, the respondent No.2 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is SCCH-10 excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 22.05.2024 at about 6.30 to 6.40 p.m.,
while the petitioner was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-J-8860 and when he reached in front of Milk Dairy, Gabbadi Village, Kanakapura - Kodihalli Road, Harohalli Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time, the driver of the Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-4898 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, as a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
6 . The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined two doctors as PW-2 and PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.29.
SCCH-10
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following:

3 9 . ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 22.05.2024.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR in crime No.0147/2024 of Harohalli PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Swift Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-AC-4898 for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
SCCH-10 Ex
.P7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Harohalli PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.7, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Sridhara, who is none other than the driver of the offending Swift Car for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPS.
10.

Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.6 produced by petitioner and discharge summaries i.e.
Ex.P.10, Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.14, it appear that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

11. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has SCCH-10 caused the accident.
12. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a Motor Vehicles Accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to CDSIMER hospital, Harohalli SCCH-10 wherein he took inpatient treatment and spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

sentences.text:
Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.6.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
16. In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P.10, Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.14.

On perusal of Ex.P.10 discharge summary of CDSIMER hospital, it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 22.05.2024 and discharged on 14.06.2024 and it also SCCH-10 discloses that, the petitioner has sustained severe traumatic brain injury and right proximal tibia fracture.
Ex . P.12
discharge summary of Sanjay Gandhi hospital it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to said hospital on 21.10.2024 and discharged on 04.11.2024.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.13 discharge summary of CDSIMER it shows that, the petitioner again admitted to said hospital on 31.12.2024 and discharged on 02.01.2025.
On perusal of Ex.P.14 discharge summary of Victoria hospital it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted on 24.06.2024 and discharged on 13.07.2024.

sentences.text: Ex.P.19 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.9,652/- and Ex.P.20 are the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills of Rs.9,652/- and same is rounded off to Rs.10,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
18. As per the medical documents it appear that, the SCCH-10 petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.

If Rs.20,000/-
is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
19. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that, due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.
In order to establish the disability, two doctors were examined before the Court as PW-2 and PW-3.
PW-2 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained severe traumatic brain injury with right proximal tibia fracture.

Further PW-2 deposed that the petitioner was treated with ICU in CDSIMER hospital and ventilator care for the head injury and the fracture was treated conservatively and taken regular follow SCCH-10 up at Victoria hospital for the right knee injury where he was diagnosed to multi ligament injury of the right knee, and hence he got admitted to Sanjay Gandhi hospital with lax knee and diagnosed to have PCL avulsion & Meniscal tear for which he underwent right knee arthroscopic debridement and PCL avulsion fixation with meniscectomy.
Further, on examination the petitioner has wasting of right muscles, restricted right knee movements and x-ray of right knee shows evidence of PCL tear repair with implant in situ.

Further deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he examined the petitioner on 17.07.2025 and the petitioner has suffered physical disability of 40% to lower limb and 13% to the whole body.

20. PW-3 Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon deposed that, the petitioner has sustained injuries to head and lost consciousness and he had scalp bleed, nasal bleed and oral bleed and on diagnose he had a GCS of E1VtM5.

Further deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he SCCH-10 examined the petitioner on 21.07.2025 and CT brain reveals diffuse cerebral atrophy along with multiple gliotic changes and old fractures of facial bones on neuro psychological assessment the petitioner obtained IQ of 74 (90-110), his ideas score was 06 suggesting a mild disability of <40%.
MMSE was done on 21.07.2025 and he had a score of 26/30.
Further deposed that the petitioner has neuro disability pertaining to cognition and total/whole body disability is around 10% and is likely to be permanent.
21. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 24 years at the time of accident and he was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m by doing executive work at Lidkar Leather Emporium, Bengaluru.
In order to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

In SCCH-10 the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,

sentences.text: Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).
The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 22.05.2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
22. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of SCCH-10 the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
23. As per the PW-2 doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 13%.
As per PW-3 Neuro Surgeon, the petitioner is suffering neuro disability of 10% to the whole body and he is likely to be permanent.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity
. The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the PW-2 has opined 13% permanent disability to the whole body and PW-3 assessed 10% disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 15%.
24. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.21.

As per Ex.P.21,
the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 03.09.2000.
The accident was SCCH-10 occurred on 22.05.2024.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 24 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 18.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 15%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,98,000/-(Rs.16,500 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,98,000/-(annual income) X 18 (multiplier) X 15% = Rs.5,34,600/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.5,34,600/-.
25.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.

Hence,
considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.

26. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;

 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 10,000/-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 20,000 /-
 Loss of Future earning Rs. 5,34,600/-
4) capacity due to permanent Mahadeva Prasad N D vs Santhosh Kumar on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78080356/

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,64,600/-.
27. REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Swift Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-4898.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of SCCH-10 the accident.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that,
the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.6,64,600/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,64,600/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

The SCCH-10 respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
